glance_takeaway: This is a post-incident report for a June 24 SEV-1 outage (INC-1194) of an Invoicing API that lasted 4h17m with a peak 31.2% API error rate, affecting 2,312 customers and ~$41,300 in SLA credits. The main message is that a bad search-query rewrite (PR #8841) was only the trigger — two dormant amplifiers (autovacuum bloat from a backfill and jitterless client retries) combined with it to saturate a shared connection pool and turn a one-endpoint slowdown into a platform-wide outage. Diagnosis, not repair, dominated the 257 minutes (68 min alert-to-diagnosis); rollback was impossible, a feature flag ended it at 17:05, no data was lost, and 3 P0 fixes land Q3 2026.

F5.note: Cause 1 detail: leading-wildcard LIKE, org scoping moved out of SQL, cost 0.56..8.44 → 6,214,891, 0.4ms → 24–31s, Rows Removed 312,344,806

F6.note: Cause 1 caveat: 'canary invoices table holds ~2M rows... seq scan takes ~180ms — under every alert threshold'

F7.note: Cause 2 detail: June 22 backfill, 38.1M dead tuples, 12.2% bloat, 190GB → 213GB, autovacuum threshold ≈54.9M on 274.2M rows

F8.note: Cause 2 detail: ~26s bloat-free estimate → 24–31s straddling the 30s statement timeout; ~57% killed (query_canceled); killed queries hold connection full 30s

F9.note: Cause 3 detail: 80-connection shared pgbouncer pool saturates 15:12, ≈5.6/s arrivals demanded 160+ connections, cl_waiting peak 1,437 at 15:58, sharing widened blast radius

F10.note: Cause 3 detail: fixed 1s interval, 3 attempts, no jitter/budget, 3,200 → 15,020 rpm (4.7x), zero extra successes, pool pinned 15:12–17:18; pool bump 80→200 at 16:20 backfired, reverted 16:31

F11.note: Diagnosis card + timeline: network hypothesis 14:20–15:10 (50 min), 14:05 provider advisory, deploy markers broken since June 10, 68 min from 14:11 alert to 15:19 diagnosis

F12.note: Rollback card: migration 0412 dropped idx_invoices_org_number, code rollback would seq-scan just the same, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY 16:05 → 21:48 (≈6h)

F13.note: Rollback card + timeline: invoice_search_contains to 0% at 17:05 after 16:35 staging verification of the untouched unique index; errors <3% by 17:15; 90-second flip; exact-match-only until June 26 re-enable

F14.note: Timeline + rollback detail: manual VACUUM 17:12–17:50 removed 38.1M dead tuples and refreshed statistics; SLOs met from 17:53; closed 18:19 after 26 min stable

F15.note: Diagnosis card: only alert was gateway 5xx > 2%/5min at 14:11; no latency SLO for invoicing though p99 exploded 14:07; 1/100 sampling (~0.7 samples/min); broken deploy marker hid the 14:02 deploy

F16.note: Actions table: all 9 items with owners and quarters; three P0s Q3 2026 (Priya N., Marcus T., Dana K.); P1s include migration-reversibility policy, autovacuum tuning, CI query-plan checks

strengths: Above-the-fold layer alone delivers all four critical takeaways: headline states the conjunction thesis, chips carry rollback-impossible/flag-fix/no-data-loss/3xP0, the causal diagram shows trigger-plus-two-amplifiers with the remove-any-leg counterfactual, and the phase strip shows where the 257 minutes went

Fact fidelity is essentially perfect: all 16 ground-truth facts present and numerically exact, including hard-to-carry details (EXPLAIN costs, cl_waiting 1,437, ~57% query_canceled, 16:35 staging verification, pool-bump reversal)

Audience fit is deliberate: every DB mechanism (B-tree/leading wildcard, dead tuples/autovacuum, covering index, pgbouncer pooling) gets a one-line gloss, exactly as the brief requires for a non-DB-specialist EM
Caveats and blameless tone preserved in dedicated caveat blocks (completed-requests latency caveat, canary blind spot, pool-bump backfire, pg_repack loose end, explicit blameless framing)

weaknesses: The full evidence lives behind collapsed <details>; a reader who never expands (or a static capture) gets only the card summaries, so depth depends on interaction — mitigated but not eliminated by Expand all

Above-the-fold density is very high (5 tiles + 4 chips + diagram + strip); appropriate for this technical audience but near the ceiling before it would become cluttered
